subject: Re: Token-flooring and request aggregation for ACME pilot
messages:
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acme-retail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Diane Procurement <diane.procure@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2028-04-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot billing question — token floors and cross-request aggregation

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — ACME's product team is excited to try Redwood in a 6-week pilot. Before procurement signs off we need to clarify how you account for small requests at high velocity. Two specific asks from our finance and engineering teams:

- If our front-end sends many tiny requests (30–80 tokens) for micro-interactions, does Redwood floor/round each request to a minimum token quantum? If so, what is the quantum and how is it applied?
- Is there a way to aggregate or bucket requests for billing (e.g., group all requests within a 1-minute window) so we don't pay per micro-call?

Understanding this is material to our TCO estimate. Diane is on this thread for procurement.

Can you send an explanation and a sample calc for 1M micro-requests/day with an assumed per-token rate? Also any options for a committed volume discount would help.

Best,
Simon
Simon Lee
Director, Platform Integrations — ACME Retail
Simon.Lee@acme-retail.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Diane Procurement <diane.procure@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — token floors and cross-request aggregation

Hi Simon —

Appreciate the detailed ask. Below is how we handle small requests today and a few options for the pilot. I attached a small CSV with worked examples.

Summary (short):
- Per-request metering: by default we meter per inference call. Each request is rounded up to the nearest 16-token quantum for billing (this prevents sub-token accounting noise).
- Prefix aggregation: we can enable a 60-second "aggregation window" on the pilot to bucket all requests from a single session/client ID and bill the aggregate tokens. This reduces the per-call floor effect but slightly increases latency for the first request while we wait to aggregate.
- Committed discount: for a 3-month pilot at a $30k/month commit we can offer a 10% unit discount and waive the per-request minimum for aggregated windows (i.e., when aggregation is on, we only round the aggregated total once).

Example calc (from the attached CSV):
Assumptions: 1,000,000 requests/day, median request payload 50 tokens (input+output combined), base rate $0.00012 per token.
- Default (no aggregation, 16-token quantum): each 50-token request rounds to 50 (already multiple of 1) — billed tokens ~= 50M tokens/day => $6,000/day.
- Fragmented micro-calls (avg 40 tokens but many at 30–80): rounding adds ~6% overhead in practice.
- Aggregation (60s window): aggregated total tokens/day ~49.6M (negligible rounding) + 10% committed discount => ~ $5,356/day.

Tradeoffs: aggregation reduces billing overhead but imposes session-scoped buffering. We can scope aggregation to a client-id (safe) and keep timeouts short (60s). For production we recommend a hybrid: enable aggregation for UI microcalls and keep low-latency direct calls for checkout flows.

Next steps I propose:
1) If this model looks acceptable, I can draft the SOW language to add an "aggregation window" flag and the pilot discount.
2) Marissa (cc'd) will confirm legal/contract language and any audit requirements.
3) If procurement needs different quantums (e.g., 50-token quantum), we can discuss but we'd prefer 16-token as our default to align with kernel batch sizing.

Attaching: metering-examples.csv and a draft SOW.

Cheers,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:55:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot billing question — token floors and cross-request aggregation

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding ACME's ask and my suggested pilot terms. Key points for internal alignment before I send the SOW:

- We default to a 16-token quantum for per-call rounding. Customer asked about larger quanta; we should avoid increasing unless the customer provides strong engineering rationale.
- For the pilot we can enable a 60s aggregation window scoped to client-id; when aggregation is active, waive per-request minimum to remove rounding noise.
- Offer: 3-month pilot, $30k/mo commit, 10% unit discount, aggregation enabled. ACME wants explicit rounding rule in writing (they asked for nearest 50 tokens in their last email reply possibility).

Questions for you:
- Marissa: can you draft SOW language that says "aggregation window will be applied per client-id; aggregated totals will be rounded once to our standard quantum (16 tokens) unless aggregation is enabled, in which case totals are rounded once per aggregation window." Also flag any audit/KYC concerns.
- Karthik: confirm that our billing system can apply aggregation windows without creating reconciliation headaches. If not, what is the implementation risk and ETA?

I attached the CSV with sample lines showing billing impact (you'll see edge-case where many 10–20 token calls produce >x% overhead).

I'll hold on sending final SOW until we confirm.

Thanks,
Rishi
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acme-retail.com>

Date: 2028-04-11T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — token floors and cross-request aggregation

Thanks Rishi — that helps a lot. ACME is agreeable to the 16-token quantum, but procurement has one request for the pilot contract: please make the rounding rule explicit and conservative — we ask that you round billed totals UP to the nearest 50-token bucket only when aggregation is OFF. If aggregation is ON (60s window) bill the aggregated total rounded up to the standard 16-token quantum once per window.

If you can add that language to the SOW and confirm the 10% pilot discount at $30k/mo, procurement will sign the pilot this week. Also please include the metering-examples.csv in the SOW appendix.

Best,
Simon

Director, Platform Integrations — ACME Retail
